problems.statement: The raw closed-ticket quota (20/day, leaderboard, non-negotiable) rewards gaming: fast link-and-solve, splitting tickets, re-solving reopened ones, and cherry-picking easy tickets. This generates its own volume, and that volume is what doubled the backlog.

Agents are not lazy and the target is not too soft. Closes per agent-day rose from 11.7 to 19.0, but much of that is non-resolution (re-solves, split children), so real resolution fell while headline output rose.
The Payroll launch is the main driver of volume and backlog growth.

Insufficient staffing or capacity is the cause, so 12 extra agents would fix it. Headcount and hours were flat, and backlog was stable at the same staffing in H1. Added capacity would feed the same distorted incentive.
Genuine first-contact demand growth is small (+4%), so it cannot explain the 66% rise in created tickets. The excess is split children (+3,470) and customer duplicates (+2,360).

Complex tickets are being starved by cherry-picking and by the quota's lack of credit for hard work, so the aged complex backlog is growing. Customers are repeatedly contacting us and CSAT is falling, with renewal risk (Larkspur).
The inflated reopen rate is a measurement artifact from an auto-reopen-on-reply rule. The rule is unchanged, and courtesy-only replies are about 5% of reopens in both periods.

Attrition and the Corvane pay competition or deferred pay review caused the backlog. Turnover was low and backfilled quickly. The survey shows rising intent to leave, which is a risk and a symptom of the quota, not a current capacity driver.
An engineering bug backlog (bank-feed sync after a partner API change) contributes to aged complex tickets and repeat contacts, but its size is unquantified.
Retention risk (58% considering leaving, 15% pay gap, pay review deferred to January) is a latent threat that could turn into a real capacity problem.

causalClaims.from: Raw daily close quota with leaderboard and no consequence for reopens
causalClaims.to: Gaming behaviours (premature solves, ticket splitting, quick-win cherry-picking)
Inflated created tickets and backlog of split children

causalClaims.from: Excluding reopened closes from the count (Team C, partial change)

causalClaims.to: Aged complex tickets and repeat contacts

actions.action: Suspend the raw closed-tickets quota and leaderboard. Replace them with a resolution-based measure (unique tickets resolved, reopens and re-solves excluded, split children counted once under the parent) plus CSAT and first-contact resolution.
actions.rationale: The quota's incentive is the established driver of the self-generated volume, and Team C and the pod show the effect of removing it.

actions.action: Make a tougher target with real consequences for misses.
actions.rationale: It would intensify gaming, worsen reopens, splits, CSAT and attrition, and would punish agents for rational responses to the incentive.

actions.action: Approve the 12 extra agents ($744k/yr, permanent) now.
actions.rationale: Staffing was not the cause. Hires would be absorbed by the same distorted incentive, and the headcount cannot be withdrawn within the fiscal year.

actions.action: Revisit headcount after 6-8 weeks of data on real first-contact resolution, unique tickets resolved and true demand under the new metric.
actions.rationale: Capacity need can only be judged once the artificial volume is stripped out.

actions.action: Run a cleanup: merge split children into parents, merge duplicates and reopened tickets, and strip them from the backlog. Then report a true backlog (about 1,100 originals plus real reopens).
actions.rationale: Much of the 3,900 is split children, duplicates and reopens, so the true workload is far smaller than it appears and the clean-up cuts it quickly.

actions.action: Run a dedicated swarm on the aged complex tickets, starting with Larkspur-type repeat cases. Restore oldest-first or priority-weighted picking, and credit effort on complex tickets.
actions.rationale: Aged complex tickets and repeat contacts drive CSAT loss and renewal risk.

actions.action: Link aged complex tickets to open engineering bugs, make the 'Waiting on engineering' status mandatory, and agree a bank-feed fix priority with Engineering.
actions.rationale: The engineering contribution is plausible but unquantified, and the linkage is cheap to establish.

actions.action: Bring forward the pay review or retention measures for agents.
actions.rationale: There is a flight risk (58% considering leaving, a competitor paying 15% more), but attrition has not driven the current backlog.

actions.action: Roll Team C's reopen-exclusion across the queue as an interim step.
actions.rationale: It cut reopens from 24% to 10%, but splits and cherry-picking continued, so it is only a partial fix.

nextEvidence: Weekly unique-ticket resolution, reopen, split and duplicate counts over the 6-8 weeks after the quota is changed, to confirm backlog stabilises and to size real capacity need
Linkage of the 430 aged complex tickets to open engineering bugs, to quantify the engineering contribution
Churn and renewal-risk data for affected customers (e.g. Larkspur) and the agent resignation trend against the Corvane pay gap
output.summary: The backlog doubled mainly because the raw close quota rewarded gaming. Agents solved prematurely, split tickets and cherry-picked easy ones. That generated reopens (6% to 23%), split children (240 to 3,710 a month) and duplicates (410 to 2,770 a month) while real first-contact demand rose only 4%. Complex tickets aged, CSAT fell and customers are at risk. Payroll, staffing, attrition and a reopen-rule change are rejected. Team C and the unquota'd pod support the incentive explanation. Remove the quota and leaderboard, measure real resolution, clean up the backlog and swarm the complex tickets. Do not tighten the target or commit to the 12 permanent hires yet.
